defaults.permitted_development: Across Surrey, agricultural buildings can benefit from Part 6 rights only where the land is a genuine agricultural unit and the proposal is reasonably necessary for agriculture. Prior approval often turns on siting, scale, design and whether the building really serves day-to-day farming rather than storage or mixed commercial use.

rules.height_rules: Across Surrey, many Part 6 schemes have to stay within a 12m overall height limit, with tighter restrictions near safeguarded aerodromes. Ridge, eaves and roof profile still have to look proportionate to the unit they serve.
rules.depth_rules: There is no householder-style depth rule. The real question is whether the span, footprint and overall scale stay reasonably necessary for the agricultural unit rather than drifting into an oversized commercial shed.
rules.boundary_rules: Across Surrey, the critical siting questions are usually proximity to roads, homes, protected buildings and open public views. Noise, odour, traffic and visual impact can all remove the comfort of relying on Part 6.
rules.roof_rules: Roof form is judged through height, bulk and the prior-approval context. Large reflective roofs or heavy ridges can be the feature that makes a building look excessive in the landscape.
rules.materials_rules: Use practical agricultural materials and muted colours that reduce glare and help the building sit quietly in the landscape rather than reading as industrial cladding.
